FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.96
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `scan_health()` marks tools as available whenever the runner function returns normally, even when the binary is missing or timed out. Evidence: `run_pyright()`, `run_ruff()`, `run_bandit()`, and `run_mypy()` all return `[]` on `_run_tool(...).stderr == "NOT_FOUND"`; `scan_health()` then sets `tools_available[tool_name] = True` unconditionally after `diags = runner(existing)`. The same false-positive availability occurs on timeout because `_run_tool()` returns a synthetic `CompletedProcess(..., returncode=-1, stderr="TIMEOUT")`, but the runners mostly just parse empty stdout and return `[]`.
FOLLOW: The endocrine layer’s primary contract is to tell the insect brain whether health tooling actually ran. With the current logic, missing/broken analyzers are reported as healthy zero-diagnostic runs. That silently degrades the “health scan” feature into dead infrastructure: reviewers see no diagnostics and no unavailable-tool signal, the insect brain cannot distinguish clean code from non-executed tools, and fix evaluation baselines that reuse these runners can also undercount issues without surfacing that the checker never ran.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — make each runner return both diagnostics and an execution-status flag, or more simply have `_run_tool()` status checked in each runner and raise/propagate a sentinel on `NOT_FOUND`/`TIMEOUT`; then set `tools_available[tool_name] = False` in `scan_health()` for those cases instead of treating empty diagnostics as success.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.93
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66
DESCRIPTION: FIND — fix evaluation test execution does not reliably run against the patched sandboxed source. In `evaluate_fix()`, the patched file is written only to `tmpdir/<basename>`, but `test_cmd` is executed unchanged via `_run_tool(test_cmd, cwd=tmpdir)`. Any command that names files by original path, imports modules from the original repo root, or runs a suite outside `tmpdir` will exercise the real source tree, not the patched file. The endocrine docstring claims sandboxing “tempdir, never modifies actual source”, but the test phase is not bound to the patched artifact.
FOLLOW: This breaks the key new capability: a fix can be labeled SAFE/HARMFUL based on tests that never touched the proposed change. Downstream, immune stage 4 imports `evaluate_fixes()` to mark findings `verified=True`; that can close bugs and activate NK “bug closed” dedup on the basis of false test evidence. In PoC terms this is high severity because it can silently produce wrong verdicts while appearing to validate end-to-end.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — before running tests, mirror the relevant source tree into the tempdir and patch the file at its relative path, then run tests from that sandbox root so imports and file references resolve to the sandboxed copy rather than the original repository.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.54
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` uses only the sum of net issue deltas, so increases in one tool can be masked by decreases in another. Evidence: `total_net = net_type_errors + net_ruff_errors + net_bandit_issues`; verdict is HARMFUL only if `total_net > 0`, SAFE if `< 0`. Example: a fix that introduces one new Bandit issue (`+1`) but removes two Ruff warnings (`-2`) yields `total_net = -1` and is classified SAFE.
FOLLOW: This violates the stated contract “SAFE: no new issues introduced”. It can mark a security-regressing or type-regressing patch as SAFE, which then propagates into immune fix verification and `verified=True` closure of the finding. That directly risks silently wrong registry state and bug-closed dedup on harmful patches.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — classify as HARMFUL if any individual net field is positive; classify as SAFE only when at least one net field is negative and none are positive; otherwise keep the existing no-change logic.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.82
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61
DESCRIPTION: FIND — the advertised defect-detection capability is only partially implemented and some declared features never fire. `DefectCategory` includes `OFF_BY_ONE` and `RACE_CONDITION`, and the module docstring promises classification for “off-by-one, race conditions”, but no categoriser path in `_categorise_pyright`, `_categorise_ruff`, `run_bandit`, or `run_mypy` ever emits those categories. `run_crosshair` is also absent despite `CROSSHAIR_BIN` and the top-level docs listing CrossHair.
FOLLOW: This creates dead feature claims in the endocrine interface. The insect brain and human reviewers may assume endocrine is monitoring those defect classes when it never can. At PoC stage that is a misleading-output problem: the feature appears present by API/docs/constants but cannot trigger, reducing trust in the health report and making debugging harder when expected categories stay permanently zero.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — remove unimplemented categories/tool claims from the endocrine interface for now, or wire the simplest real implementation: add a `run_crosshair()` path and only keep categories that current tool parsers can actually emit.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.79
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.43
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `health_trend()` returns ragged per-category histories and omits zero counts for rounds where a category did not appear. Evidence: it iterates `for scan in self._scan_history: for cat, count in scan.counts_by_category.items(): trend.setdefault(cat, []).append(count)`. If a category is absent in a round, no `0` is appended, so list positions no longer align to round indices.
FOLLOW: Any consumer comparing round-over-round trends can misread category trajectories because list index is not stable across rounds. A category sequence like `[5, 1]` may mean rounds 0 and 2, not consecutive rounds. That makes worsening/improving-health logic unreliable and can mis-trigger or miss pacing or human review decisions based on trends.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — build trends over all known categories across all scans and append `scan.counts_by_category.get(cat, 0)` for every round so each category history has one entry per scan.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F006
SEVERITY: 0.74
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.48
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `compute_pacing_signals()` claims `context_budget: int` but contains runtime handling for `dict`, then immediately compares `if context_budget > 0:` and divides by it. This is an interface mismatch with the function signature and datamodel. The defensive dict branch implies callers may pass per-model budgets, but the function collapses them to `max(...)`, which understates pressure for smaller-budget models.
FOLLOW: Downstream pacing decisions can be silently wrong in multi-model runs with budget overrides: the endocrine signal may report context as healthy because it uses the largest budget, while one or more models are already near exhaustion. That weakens the insect brain’s degrade/relay decisions and makes the signal misleading.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — make the interface honest: accept only an integer budget in this function and remove the dict branch; callers should pass the actual effective budget they want evaluated.
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F007
SEVERITY: 0.71
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.37
DESCRIPTION: FIND — slow-model and response-size “median” calculations use `sorted(values)[len(values)//2]`, which is not the statistical median for even-sized sets. With 4 or 6 models this selects the upper middle value rather than the average of the two middles. In a 5-model system this is usually fine, but the code is generic and the endocrine layer is infrastructure.
FOLLOW: Threshold-based pacing signals can shift materially around the trigger boundary, especially with an even number of active models after failures. That can suppress legitimate slow-model/context-growth signals or emit spurious ones, affecting relay degradation and timeout adjustments.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — use `statistics.median()` for durations and response sizes.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F008
SEVERITY: 0.69
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.41
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_find_target_file()` matches on `if sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path`, so a short substring from a finding/proposed fix can select the wrong file when multiple source paths contain that fragment. Because it falls back to the first source path, ambiguous or missing references are also silently coerced to an arbitrary file.
FOLLOW: Fix evaluation may patch and analyze the wrong file while still producing a concrete SAFE/HARMFUL verdict. That contaminates pre/post counts, test results, and any downstream `verified=True` marking in the immune pipeline. Silent mis-targeting is worse than UNEVALUABLE because it looks authoritative.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — require an unambiguous exact basename or normalized relative-suffix match to one source path; if multiple paths match or none match, return `None` so the evaluation is marked UNEVALUABLE instead of patching an arbitrary file.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F009
SEVERITY: 0.63
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.35
DESCRIPTION: FIND — CrossHair and Python 3.13 interpreter constants are declared but unused in endocrine health scan and fix evaluation paths. The module header lists CrossHair among tool binaries and capabilities, but no code path invokes it, and `PYTHON_313` is never referenced.
FOLLOW: This is dead code plus misleading capability advertisement. For a PoC, dead declarations by themselves are low, but here they reinforce a false impression that symbolic execution is part of the health monitor when it never contributes diagnostics or fix evaluation. That can misdirect debugging and review effort.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — remove the unused constants and CrossHair mentions until a real invocation path exists.
VERIFIED: TRUE
